query: UPDATE services SET faqs = '[{"q":"How do I know if my basement has a water problem or just condensation?","a":"Condensation forms on cold surfaces like pipes and walls when warm humid air hits them. You can test the difference by taping a piece of plastic sheeting to the wall and sealing the edges. If moisture appears on the room side of the plastic after a day or two, it is condensation. If moisture appears on the wall side, water is coming through the foundation. Most wet basements in London Ontario involve actual water intrusion, not just condensation."},{"q":"What causes wet basements in London Ontario specifically?","a":"London sits on clay-heavy soil that expands when wet and contracts when dry. This movement puts pressure on foundation walls over time, causing cracks. Many homes in older London neighbourhoods like Old North, Byron, and Old South were built before modern waterproofing standards, and their drainage systems are aging. Spring snowmelt and heavy rainfall events are the most common triggers for basement flooding in this area."},{"q":"Is a wet basement covered by home insurance in Ontario?","a":"It depends on the cause. Sudden and accidental water damage from a burst pipe or a one-time sewer backup is usually covered. Gradual seepage through foundation cracks or chronic drainage problems is typically excluded as a maintenance issue. If you have overland flood coverage or sewer backup coverage as add-ons to your policy, those may apply. Always check your specific policy and call your insurer before doing repairs."},{"q":"What is the difference between interior and exterior waterproofing?","a":"Exterior waterproofing involves excavating around the foundation, applying a waterproof membrane to the outside of the wall, and installing new drainage tile. It addresses the problem at the source but is more disruptive and expensive. Interior waterproofing involves installing a drainage channel along the interior perimeter of the basement floor, directing water to a sump pump. It does not stop water from entering the wall but manages it before it reaches the floor. Both approaches are legitimate depending on the situation."},{"q":"How long does a wet basement repair take?","a":"Most interior waterproofing jobs in a typical London home take one to two days. Exterior waterproofing that requires excavation can take three to five days depending on the size of the foundation and site access. Crack injection repairs are usually completed in a few hours. We will give you a clear timeline before work begins."},{"q":"What is the 20-year warranty on wet basement repairs?","a":"Our wet basement waterproofing work is backed by a written 20-year warranty. If the repaired area develops a water problem within that period, we come back and fix it at no charge. The warranty is transferable to new owners if you sell the home, which can be a selling point."},{"q":"Can tree roots cause a wet basement?","a":"Yes. Tree roots can crack foundation walls and drainage tile over time. They can also block the weeping tile around your foundation, preventing proper drainage and causing water to build up against the wall. If you have large trees close to your house, root intrusion is worth investigating as part of any basement water assessment."},{"q":"Should I use a sump pump or waterproofing, or both?","a":"A sump pump removes water that has already entered the drainage system. Waterproofing prevents or manages water before it reaches the living space. In many cases, both are used together. The sump pump handles the water collected by the interior drainage channel, and the waterproofing membrane or crack repairs reduce the amount of water getting in. We assess each situation individually and recommend what is actually needed."},{"q":"How much does wet basement repair cost in Ontario?","a":"Costs vary significantly depending on the method and the size of the problem. Crack injection repairs typically range from a few hundred to around a thousand dollars per crack. Interior drainage systems for a full basement can range from several thousand to over ten thousand dollars. Exterior excavation and waterproofing is generally the most expensive option. We provide written quotes before any work begins so there are no surprises."},{"q":"What is weeping tile and does my house have it?","a":"Weeping tile is a perforated pipe installed around the perimeter of a foundation to collect groundwater and direct it away from the house. Most homes built in London after the 1950s have some form of weeping tile, though older systems used clay tile that can crack, collapse, or become blocked with roots over time. A camera inspection can determine whether your weeping tile is functioning properly."},{"q":"Can I waterproof a basement myself?","a":"Some minor crack repairs can be done with hydraulic cement or epoxy injection kits available at hardware stores. However, these are surface fixes and may not address the underlying cause. For persistent or widespread water problems, professional assessment is recommended. Improper repairs can mask the problem temporarily while allowing damage to continue behind the walls."},{"q":"Does a wet basement affect the structural integrity of my home?","a":"Over time, yes. Water that repeatedly saturates the soil around a foundation can cause settling and movement. Chronic moisture weakens mortar joints in block foundations and can cause bowing or cracking in poured concrete walls. If you are seeing horizontal cracks in a block foundation wall, that is a structural concern that should be assessed promptly."},{"q":"What should I do immediately if my basement floods?","a":"First, make sure it is safe to enter. If there is any possibility of electrical hazards, stay out and call an electrician or emergency services. Once it is safe, remove standing water as quickly as possible using a wet-dry vacuum or pump. Move belongings to dry areas and start fans and dehumidifiers to prevent mould. Document the damage with photos for insurance purposes. Then call us to assess the source of the problem so it does not happen again."}]' WHERE slug = 'wet-basement-repair';
